facts.fact_text: A demonstration was planned to be held in Baku on 12 January 2013.
A demonstration was planned to be held in Baku on 26 January 2013.
A demonstration was planned to be held in Baku on 10 March 2013.
A demonstration was planned to be held in Baku on 29 December 2013.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were conducted in a peaceful manner.
The demonstration of 12 January 2013 was aimed at protesting about the deaths of soldiers in the army.
The demonstration of 10 March 2013 was aimed at protesting about the deaths of soldiers in the army.
The demonstration of 26 January 2013 condemned the use of force by the police against the participants of previous demonstrations.

Those taking part in the demonstration of 29 December 2013 were protesting against bureaucratic injustices which had allegedly caused a disabled war veteran to set himself on fire on 25 December 2013.
Each applicant attended one of the demonstrations as specified in the Appendix.
Shortly after the demonstrations had begun, the police started to disperse those who had gathered.
All the applicants were arrested during the dispersal operations.
All the applicants were taken to various police stations following their arrest.
On the day of each applicant's arrest, administrative offence reports (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) were issued.
The administrative offence reports stated that the applicants had committed an administrative offence under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
According to most of the applicants, they were not given access to a lawyer after their arrest.
According to most of the applicants, they were not given access to a lawyer while they were in police custody.
The applicant in application no. 20589/13 was released after being kept in police custody for a few hours, subject to an undertaking to reappear at the police station on various dates.
The applicant in application no. 26424/14 was released after being kept in police custody for a few hours, subject to an undertaking to reappear at the police station on various dates.
Most of the applicants were taken to trial courts directly from the police stations.
Most of the applicants were taken to trial courts either on the day of their arrest or the following day.
The first-instance courts found that the applicants had participated in unauthorised demonstrations.
The applicants were convicted under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The applicants were sentenced to a period of administrative detention varying from thirteen to seventeen days, or to a fine of 400 or 500 Azerbaijani manats (AZN), as specified in the Appendix.
It appears that the organisers of the demonstrations gave no proper prior notice to the relevant authority, the Baku City Executive Authority.
At the time of the applicants' arrest, Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that no prior written notification was required for spontaneous assemblies.

Before amendments introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, a breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies was punishable under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 entered into force on 1 January 2013.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced new wording to Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences on breaching the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies.

Following the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, participation in an assembly organised in breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies became explicitly punishable under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

Following the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, punishments in the form of administrative detention of up to 15 days were introduced for the first time under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
